The statement balances strong labor-market data with elevated inflation and geopolitical supply shocks. Consistent with Phillips-curve/New Keynesian frameworks, higher energy prices and war-related disruptions worsen the short-run output–inflation trade-off, implying that some tightening is needed to contain inflation pressures. By initiating liftoff and signaling balance-sheet reduction, the Committee is acting in line with inflation-targeting and expectations-based policy literature: credible, systematic firming helps anchor expected inflation near the 2 percent objective, mitigating longer-run welfare costs and reducing the real costs of disinflation compared with delayed action. Near term, theory and evidence suggest tighter policy will weigh on activity, but a strong labor market provides resilience. Net tone: cautiously constructive on medium-term inflation control, tempered by near-term downside risks to growth and upside risks to inflation.
